headline: UK Consumer Confidence Tumbles at Fastest Pace Outside Pandemic Since 2016
summary: UK consumer confidence plummeted at its steepest rate outside the pandemic since the 2016 Brexit referendum, weighed down by escalating Middle East conflict and cost-of-living strains ahead of the government's budget.
why: Consumer spending represents over 60% of UK gross domestic product. Deteriorating sentiment typically translates into weaker retail sales, lower hospitality receipts, and softer economic growth.

impacts.name: Consumer Discretionary
impacts.why: Declining consumer morale prompts household thrift, dampening non-essential retail and hospitality revenues.
